title: Route MPD credentials through the typed secret broker
description:
## Finding

`[media.mpd].password` bypasses the repository's completed typed credential-broker chokepoint. It is modeled, serialized, lowered, cloned, debug-formatted, and consumed as an ordinary `Option<String>`. It is absent from the canonical secret inventory, so plaintext validation, `thegn secret list/audit/migrate`, doctor presence reporting, keyring references, resolution outcome auditing, and metadata-only consumer attribution do not cover it.

The standard `password@host` form accepted from `MPD_HOST` is also parsed inside the leaf media crate and becomes an unaudited raw string. A configured but missing credential cannot be distinguished from no credential through the broker contract.

## Evidence at `299fc13ee53f31bdeb99bbf35609a6ad55528973`

* `crates/thegn-core/src/config_media.rs:15-29`: `MpdMediaConfig` derives `Debug` and serializes `password: Option<String>`; a pasted password remains in `config.toml`.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/config_media.rs:43-69`: config lowering clones the plaintext value into `thegn_media::ResolveOpts` without host-side typed resolution or an audit event.
* `crates/thegn-media/src/lib.rs:281-295`: `ResolveOpts` also derives `Debug` and stores the password as an ordinary clonable string.
* `crates/thegn-media/src/mpd.rs:26-31`: `MpdEndpoint` derives `Debug` while retaining another cloned `Option<String>`.
* `crates/thegn-media/src/mpd.rs:48-77`: `MPD_HOST=password@host` is split in the leaf and the raw password is retained directly.
* `crates/thegn-media/src/lib.rs:439-450`: backend construction passes that cleartext value to the endpoint without the host credential resolver.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/secret_scan.rs:28-112`: the canonical inventory claims to enumerate every configured secret but covers provider, issue, CI, VPN, snapshot, and MCP fields only; media MPD is absent.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/secret_scan.rs:157-166`: plaintext migration warnings cover only issue-account and GitLab token literals. An MPD password literal is invisible.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/secret.rs:48-88`: `resolve_ref_for` is the intended single host-side resolution/audit chokepoint, but this consumer never calls it.

## Impact

Users are encouraged to place a reusable daemon password directly in a broadly read configuration file or environment string. They cannot store it in the OS keyring through the advertised reference syntax, migrate it with the secret CLI, verify its presence with doctor, or audit when the media subsystem used it. Derived `Debug` implementations create latent accidental-disclosure paths, and repeated clones expand the cleartext lifetime and number of memory locations.

This also breaks the architectural assertion that the canonical scanner knows every configured secret and that every non-empty resolution emits one metadata-only audit record.

## Required design

1. Model `media.mpd.password` as a typed `SecretRef` at the host boundary with explicit legacy bare-string-as-literal compatibility.
2. Add the field to `secret_refs`, plaintext detection, doctor/list/audit/migrate, schema/docs, and config rewrite logic under a stable `media:mpd` consumer tag.
3. Resolve only through the installed host broker and preserve distinct unconfigured, missing, unavailable, and resolved outcomes. An explicitly configured missing secret must not silently become anonymous/no-auth operation.
4. Move `MPD_HOST` credential parsing/resolution to an audited host boundary. Preserve endpoint compatibility, but deprecate or safely represent embedded credentials without exposing values in diagnostics.
5. Use a non-`Debug`, non-displayable secret wrapper with zeroization/ownership semantics across the minimal lifetime needed for authentication. Avoid unrestricted `Clone` of secret-bearing endpoint/options structs, or implement narrowly scoped secret cloning with reviewable ownership.
6. Ensure serialization emits only the reference, never a resolved value. Error, trace, config-health, and schema paths must not reveal secret contents or a password-bearing `MPD_HOST`.
7. Add deterministic tests for literal/env/file/keyring references, missing/unavailable backends, migration, exactly-one metadata-only audit event, config round-trip, debug/redaction, embedded-host compatibility, and memory cleanup where observable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] MPD appears in the canonical secret inventory and all secret CLI/doctor surfaces.
- [ ] A legacy literal is warned and can be migrated without breaking authentication.
- [ ] Keyring, env, and file references resolve through the broker with consumer `media:mpd`.
- [ ] Explicit resolution failure is typed and cannot silently attempt an unauthenticated connection.
- [ ] No normal `Debug`, display, trace, config serialization, or error path can expose the password.
- [ ] Resolved credential material has one bounded owner/lifetime and is zeroized on release.
- [ ] Tests prove exactly-one audit attribution and absence of value-bearing output.

## Dependency map

* Related to <issue id="8d90bd35-b00a-4c4c-9554-240a4750967e" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-122/complete-credential-broker-rollout-and-managed-ssh-key-custody">THE-122</issue>: this is a missed secret consumer discovered after that rollout was marked complete and must preserve its canonical broker/audit model.
* Related to <issue id="c1894b1e-5842-4f35-a447-64783f268356" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-486/route-calendar-account-secrets-through-the-typed-credential-broker">THE-486</issue>: calendar accounts have the same post-rollout raw-secret bypass; shared scanner/migration work should not create divergent semantics.
* Related to <issue id="fc3a19c9-440d-4da3-a991-ec5a85d60e66" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-490/bound-and-validate-mpd-protocol-framing-commands-and-endpoints">THE-490</issue>: protocol argument validation remains mandatory after broker resolution, and endpoint diagnostics must redact embedded credentials.
* Independent of MPD state/capability correctness; credential custody and runtime truthfulness can be implemented and reviewed separately.
